sentences.text: Once upon a time, a simple man lived in a small town named Swaffham.
His name was John, and he worked hard as a traveler to make money for his family.
Although his life was difficult, John tried to keep a good heart.
He walked from house to house every single day, trying to sell small things to people.
He wanted to provide a good life for everyone in his home, but money was always tight.
Sometimes he felt very tired, yet he never stopped walking because his family needed food.
Every evening he returned with very little coin, but he always smiled at his children.
His wife would look at him with love, knowing how hard he worked during those long hours.
They hoped that one day their situation would improve, bringing happiness and rest.
Life in the town was quiet, and most people knew each other quite well.
John was known as an honest person who always kept his word to his friends.
No one had any bad thing to say about him, because he was always kind.
However, his pockets remained mostly empty, and winter was coming soon.
The cold weather would make travel much harder, increasing their daily worries.
John often sat by the fire, wondering how they would survive the coming months.
He prayed for some good change to change their life and save them from poverty.
If he had more money, they would not worry about the cold.
If the winter were shorter, life would be much easier for everyone in the house.
One night, John had a very strange dream while he was sleeping in his bed.
In his dream, a voice told him that if he went to London bridge, a great fortune would be found there.
The voice spoke clearly, and the image stayed in his mind for many days.
At first, John thought the dream meant nothing, but it kept coming back to him again and again.
He tried to ignore the thought, but it grew stronger inside his head each morning.
Could the dream be real, or was it just another trick of his tired mind?
He discussed the matter with his wife, who listened carefully to every word.
She suggested that perhaps he should make the journey to see what might happen.
After much thought, the traveler decided to leave his home and walk all the way to London.
It took him several days to reach the big city, which was full of noise and strange people.
When John arrived at London bridge, he found that it was covered with shops and crowded with traffic.
He spent a whole day walking across the bridge, waiting and watching for the wealth that the voice had promised.
Nothing happened during the afternoon, and the sun began to go down.
John felt very tired, and his feet hurt from so much walking.
If he had stayed at home, his feet would not hurt so much.
If the bridge were empty, he would find the gold faster.
As he sat near a market to rest, the store owner came outside and asked him why he was there.
The friendly manager looked closely at the tired traveler and wanted to know his story.
John decided to tell the truth about his strange dream.
He explained how a voice had told him to come to London bridge for a great fortune.
When the store owner heard this, he began to laugh out loud.
The man shook his head and told John that silly dreams should never be followed.
The man said that he himself had dreamed of a house in Swaffham.
In that dream, a traveler named John had a hidden gold box under his bed.
He laughed again, saying that if he were silly like John, he would spend his time digging up every garden.
When John heard those words, his heart gave a big jump.
He knew immediately that the house the man spoke of was his own home.
Without wasting a single minute, the happy traveler thanked the man and turned back toward his town.
If the store owner had not spoken, John would never have known the truth.
If he had not traveled to London, the secret would have remained hidden.
He walked home as fast as he could, feeling full of energy and hope.
When John finally arrived back at his house, he took some tools and began to dig under his bed.
Deep in the ground, a massive box of gold and silver coins was discovered at last.
The discovery brought a wonderful new life to his family.
They were finally rich, and all their money problems disappeared completely.
John bought food, clothes, and a better house for his family.
They never had to worry about the cold winter or lack of food again.
The strange dream had changed everything, proving that sometimes good things really do happen.
People in the town talked about the amazing event for many years later.
John lived a long, happy life, always remembering the voice that sent him to London.
If they had been poor forever, they would not have bought a new house.
If John had ignored the dream, the gold would still be under the floor.

A big ship crossing the sea
A golden crown lost in a river

options: Under his own bed in Swaffham

sentences.text: In the quiet market town of Swaffham, where the mist clung stubbornly to the damp thatch of the roofs, there lived a humble peddler named John.
Day after day, driven by an unyielding sense of duty, he walked the winding country lanes to earn a meager living for his household.
Though his physical frame was constantly fatigued by the endless miles, he maintained a gentle spirit that endeared him to his neighbors.
He carried a pack filled with small trinkets and household necessities, hoping against hope that his labor might yield enough coin to secure their daily bread.
His devoted wife met him each evening with a tender look, fully aware of the toll those grueling hours took upon his weary limbs.
Poverty cast a long, cold shadow over their modest hearth, and the approaching winter promised trials far harsher than they had yet endured.
Had they possessed even a small reserve of wealth, the impending frost would not have filled their minds with such persistent dread.
John often sat by the dying embers of the fire, pondering how they would survive the bleak months ahead without falling deeper into debt.
He was known throughout the parish as a man of absolute integrity, whose word was never broken and whose kindness never wavered.
Yet honesty alone could not purchase firewood, nor could his spotless reputation put food upon the bare wooden table for his children.
One restless night, as sleep finally overtook his exhausted mind, John experienced a remarkably vivid and unusual dream.
A disembodied voice echoed through the vast emptiness of his slumber, declaring with absolute certainty that a great fortune awaited him at London Bridge.
Not only did the pronouncement ring with startling clarity, but the image of the distant bridge embedded itself deeply within his consciousness.
When morning arrived, he initially dismissed the vision as a mere phantom born of exhaustion and nightly anxiety.
Day after day, however, the mysterious command returned to haunt his thoughts, growing increasingly difficult to ignore.
Could the nocturnal whisper possibly hold a kernel of truth, or was it merely another cruel trick played by a desperate imagination?
Unable to bear the uncertainty any longer, he confided the entire strange occurrence to his wife, watching her face for any sign of doubt.
She listened intently to every syllable, her practical mind weighing the slim possibilities against the crushing reality of their destitute state.
It was she who finally suggested that he undertake the long journey southward to discover what fate might have in store for him.
After much anxious deliberation, the traveler resolved to leave his familiar surroundings and walk all the way to the sprawling capital.
It took him several grueling days of steady travel to reach the outskirts of London, a city that overwhelmed his rustic senses with its deafening roar.
When John finally stepped onto London Bridge, he found himself entirely unprepared for the chaotic spectacle unfolding before his eyes.
The ancient stone structure was packed tightly with small shops and blocked by a relentless stream of carts, merchants, and pedestrians.
For hours he wandered back and forth across the crowded span, watching anxiously for any sign of the promised wealth.
Had the bridge been mercifully empty, or had he arrived at a quieter hour, his task might have proved far less daunting.
As the afternoon waned and shadows lengthened across the river Thames, John sought refuge near a bustling market stall to ease his aching feet.
Had he chosen to remain safely at home in Swaffham, his weary joints would not have throbbed with such sharp, unrelenting pain.
The proprietor of the shop, a sharp-eyed yet fundamentally kind-hearted merchant, noticed the traveler slumped against a wooden post.
Intrigued by the man's profound exhaustion and forlorn expression, the store owner approached him and gently inquired about the purpose of his visit.
Hesitant at first, John eventually decided to confide the whole truth, recounting the peculiar dream that had driven him hundreds of miles from home.
Scarcely had the peddler finished describing the mysterious voice than the merchant burst into a loud, hearty fit of laughter.
Shaking his head at the naive simplicity of the traveler, the store manager advised him never to place any faith in foolish nighttime visions.
The merchant declared that he himself had recently suffered through a remarkably persistent dream concerning a remote house in distant Swaffham.
In that nocturnal fantasy, according to the shopkeeper, a humble peddler named John possessed a massive chest of gold buried beneath his own bed.
The store owner chuckled, adding that if he were gullible enough to chase such nonsense, he would spend every waking moment digging up random gardens.
Upon hearing those extraordinary words, John felt his heart leap violently against his ribs as a sudden revelation struck him with blinding force.
He instantly recognized the precise dwelling the merchant described as his own modest cottage back in Swaffham.
Had the friendly store owner kept his thoughts to himself, the secret would have remained forever buried beneath the floorboards.
Without wasting a single precious moment, the overjoyed traveler thanked the merchant profusely and turned his footsteps back toward the north.
Had he not undertaken the arduous pilgrimage to London, the golden hoard would have slumbered in darkness for the rest of his natural days.
Fueled by a sudden surge of adrenaline and boundless hope, he traversed the long road homeward with a lightness in his step he had not felt in years.
When John finally crossed the threshold of his familiar cottage, he immediately gathered the necessary tools to begin his clandestine excavation.
Beneath the sleeping quarters, deep in the dark earth, his shovel struck something hard and metallic with a dull, echoing thud.
With trembling hands, he uncovered a massive chest overflowing with heavy gold and silver coins that glittered softly in the dim light.
The staggering discovery swept away the dark cloud of poverty that had hung over his family for generations.
Instantly, their precarious existence was transformed into one of comfort, security, and quiet abundance.
John purchased wholesome food, fine garments, and a much sturdier house where his children could grow without the constant terror of the winter cold.
Had they remained destitute forever, they never would have known the sweet relief of financial peace and proper shelter.
For decades afterward, townsfolk whispered in awe about the miraculous chain of events that had brought sudden wealth to the honest peddler.
John lived out his remaining years in serene contentment, frequently marveling at the mysterious voice that had directed him all the way to London.
